Download CVR documents

Source: R/cvr.R
cvr_download.Rd

Downloads the documents listed in a tibble from cvr_hits(), one file per row. A delay between requests keeps the load on the API polite.

Usage

cvr_download(hits, path, sleep = 3, overwrite = FALSE, name_by = "cvrnummer")

Arguments

hits

A tibble with cvrnummer and dokumenturl columns, typically from cvr_hits().

path

Directory to download into. Created automatically if it does not exist.

sleep

Seconds to wait between downloads. Must be at least 1; the default of 3 matches the API's expectations for bulk retrieval.

overwrite

What to do about files that already exist. FALSE (default) aborts before downloading anything; "skip" leaves them alone and fetches the rest, which is how an interrupted bulk download is resumed; TRUE replaces them.

name_by

Columns of hits to build each file name from, joined with _. Defaults to the CVR number alone, which means a company's filings for different years are told apart only by a _2, _3 suffix in whatever order the API returned them. Pass c("cvrnummer", "slutdato") to name them by period instead.

Value

hits with two columns added: path, the file each row was written to, and downloaded, whether it arrived. Rows that failed keep their path, so a second attempt can select them.

Details

Each company-year typically lists several files (PDF, XML/XBRL, sometimes XHTML), so filter the hits tibble before downloading if you only need one format, e.g. hits[hits$dokumentmimetype == "application/xml", ].

See also

cvr_query(), cvr_search(), cvr_hits(), and read_xbrl() for the machine-readable filings. A PDF filing has no parser here; it goes through taxmill.

Other cvr: cvr_hits(), cvr_query(), cvr_search()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
files <- cvr_query("12345678", "2024-01-01", "2024-12-31") |>
  cvr_search(contact = "you@example.com") |>
  cvr_hits() |>
  cvr_download("data/pdf")

files[!files$downloaded, ]
} # }
